issue.title: Waiter agent fails with NameCollisionError at wake after a long wait, and nothing retries it
issue.description: The sase-11l.6 waiter waited 41 hours; when its dependency epic sase-11l.5.1 was manually closed at 2026-09-18 06:18 EDT it woke and immediately failed with NameCollisionError: agent name 'sase-11l.6' is already taken, requiring a manual epic relaunch at 06:21. The week's notification history shows the same failure class on 08-03 and 08-14. Root cause not yet diagnosed - plausibly a stale name reservation from the original launch or a prior shell surviving in the registry - but the pattern is clear: the longer a waiter sleeps, the likelier its wake-time launch collides, and a wake-time failure has no automatic retry, so long waits convert into permanent stalls that look like ordinary WAITING rows until someone digs.

task_type_fields.impact: Long-waiting epic dependents die at the exact moment they become runnable, silently re-stalling the epic a human just unblocked
task_type_fields.location: agent launch name reservation / waiter wake path (exact locus undiagnosed)
task_type_fields.repro: Let a %w waiter outlive its original launch context by many hours, then satisfy its dependency; wake launch fails NameCollisionError (sase-11l.6 after 41h, 2026-09-18 06:18 EDT; prior on 08-03 and 08-14)
